newsitem.title: USA: NY officers may face civil rights charges.
newsitem.headline: NY officers may face civil rights charges.

text.p: Two New York City police officers indicted for allegedly assaulting and sodomizing a man in custody with a toilet plunger could also face federal civil rights charges, officials said Monday.
U.S. Attorney Zachary Carter told reporters that authorities in New York were working with the civil rights division of the Justice Depoartment in Washington on a preliminary investigation.

"Among the most disturbing aspects is that one or more officers are alleged to have commmitted an act of almost incomprehensible depravity within a police precinct in apparent expectation that they could get away with it," Carter said.

The alleged attack Aug. 9 on a Haitian immigrant in the bathroom of the 70th precinct house in Brooklyn has highlighted three years of accusations by minority communities that in their successful campaign to combat city crime, police have become more abusive.
Security guard Abner Louima, 30, was taken into custody after a brawl outside a nightclub.

Indictments against Officers Charles Schwarz, 31, and Officer Justin Volpe, 25, were formally unsealed Monday in State Supreme Court in Brooklyn. They are charged with aggravated sexual abuse and first degree assault. They face a maximum of 25 years in prison if convicted. Both denied the charges and have been released on bail of $100,000 each.
An attorney for Schwarz said his client was "the wrong man" and suggested that the investigation to find the culprits was out of control.
"This investigation has been recklessly moved forward," attorney Stephen Worth said. "I asked the court not to be swept up in the same hysteria as the district attorney's office is."

In the days since the incident shocked the city, Brooklyn District Attorney Charles Hines pressed charges, while Mayor Rudolph Giuliani and Police Commissioner Howard Safir cleaned out the precinct house where the alleged attack took place.

Eighteen officers from the precinct have been placed on desk duty, suspended, arrested or transferred in the sweep by Giuliani, the man most closely identified with reducing city crime to its lowest levels in a generation.

Louima remains in stable but critical condition in the hospital. He suffered a tear in his colon, bruises of the bladder, the loss of teeth and a possible fracture of the lower jaw. Louima accused his captors of kicking him and beating him with police radios before taking him to the precinct house.
